themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1500% increase (z-score: 11.62)—suggesting a coordinated or sudden surge in illicit signage, graffiti postings, or unauthorized advertising across Queens Village/Cambria Heights this week.
evidence: 6 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 11.62 indicates statistically extreme deviation
No prior Reddit or news coverage of posting issue suggests this is a new neighborhood problem
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: visit affected blocks to photograph and document the nature of postings (political, commercial, gang-related?)
Source investigation: interview NYPD and Parks Enforcement to determine if this reflects enforcement action or actual surge in illegal posting activity

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Overgrowth Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Two tree-related 311 spikes converged this week: Illegal Tree Damage (4 complaints last week, up 357% from 0.9 avg) and Overgrown Tree/Branches (16 complaints THIS WEEK, up 184% from 5.6 avg), suggesting either storm damage, lack of maintenance, or deliberate tree vandalism affecting neighborhood infrastructure and pedestrian safety.
evidence: 16 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.6 weekly average (184% spike, z-score: 4.33)
4 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (357% spike, z-score: 5.21)
Community board has repeatedly requested 'Better Park Maintenance' and park/amenity upgrades, indicating chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Investigate Parks Department tree maintenance schedule and budget allocation for CD 413—are crews understaffed or underfunded?
Document specific streets/parks with dangerous overgrowth; interview residents about safety hazards (blocked sidewalks, downed branches near power lines)
Examine whether recent weather events (high winds, storms) triggered spike or if this reflects systemic maintenance gap

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 9 last week from a baseline of 1.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 500% spike (z-score: 7.5)—indicating a potential pest crisis or favorable conditions for rodent breeding across the district.
evidence: 9 rodent complaints last week vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase, z-score: 7.5)
Spike coincides with warm weather window and potential delayed response to fall/winter breeding cycle
No prior news coverage or Reddit mentions—indicates undetected neighborhood problem
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Health Department about rodent pressure and extermination capacity in CD 413
Canvass affected blocks to identify common sources: inadequate waste management, open food waste, or building code violations enabling rodent entry
Examine whether this correlates with street condition complaints (2208 over 90 days)—poor street maintenance creates habitat for rodents

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials & Asbestos Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Two environmental health spikes emerged 2 weeks ago: Hazardous Materials (4 complaints, up 433% from 0.8 avg, z-score: 4.91) and Asbestos (3 complaints, up 700% from 0.4 avg, z-score: 3.77), suggesting either active demolition/construction without proper abatement oversight or discovery of legacy contamination in older housing stock.
evidence: 4 hazardous materials complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score: 4.91)
3 asbestos complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 3.77)
247-56 90th Ave rezoning is in public review phase—potential construction/demolition activity triggering contamination complaints
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 hazmat/asbestos complaints with DOB Building Permits and ULURP timeline to determine if rezoning/demolition activity is driving spikes
Investigate whether complaint locations cluster around specific properties or construction sites
Interview EPA and NYC Department of Environmental Protection about asbestos notification and abatement procedures for this district

themes_detail.label: Street & Infrastructure Decay Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street condition remains the top 311 complaint category (2208 over 90 days), and curb condition complaints spiked to 6 last week from 1.0 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 4.08), alongside long-standing community board budget requests for street reconstruction—evidence of chronic deferred maintenance now accelerating.
evidence: Street condition: 2,208 complaints over 90 days (highest volume category)
Curb condition: 6 complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (500% spike, z-score: 4.08)
Community board has requested street reconstruction funding year-over-year, indicating unsolved chronic problem
reporting_angles: Obtain DOT street inspection data for CD 413—what percentage of streets are rated poor/fair condition, and what is the backlog for repairs?
Map curb damage complaints geographically to identify problem corridors; interview residents about impacts (mobility hazards, vehicle damage, water pooling)
Investigate whether recent snow/ice complaints (1,197 over 90 days) exacerbated underlying street decay
